candidates.lead: Healthcare worker pay in Australia is set by state enterprise agreements for public-sector nurses and midwives, and by federal awards such as the Nurses Award 2020 (MA000034) for private hospitals, GP clinics and aged care. Across the eight state scales a registered nurse's entry step runs from $74,831 in SA to $84,188 in Victoria [[registeredNurseRange]]; the award minimum is $1,219.50 a week from 1 July 2026.

A nurse's pay in Australia depends on the state, because each public health system has its own agreement and classification ladder. Entry-step registered nurse pay runs from $74,831 a year in SA to $84,188 in Victoria, and the top of the base scale from $102,103 to $115,682 [[registeredNurseRange]], before shift penalties. The Nurses Award 2020 floor is $32.09 an hour from 1 July 2026 [[NURSES_AWARD]].

Healthcare pay covers nurses, midwives, doctors, allied health and aged care workers, each on a different scale: state enterprise agreements in public hospitals and federal awards elsewhere. A registered nurse starts between $74,831 (SA) and $84,188 (VIC) a year on the 2026 state scales [[registeredNurseRange]]; the Nurses Award 2020 (MA000034) minimum is $1,219.50 a week from 1 July 2026 [[NURSES_AWARD]].
